value: Azure Automation State Configuration for now; it retires on 30 September 2027, so plan a move to Azure Machine Configuration.
reason: The page now carries an end-of-life note: State Configuration retires on 30 September 2027 and users should transition to Machine Configuration, itself a defensible answer.

value: It scales across thousands of machines from one central location with compliance reports, but Microsoft asks users to move to Machine Configuration before it retires.
reason: Explains the retirement caveat added to the back.

value: It imports DSC resources and assigns configurations in the cloud, but it retires on 30 September 2027, with Azure Machine Configuration named as its successor.
reason: The overview's end-of-life note (30 September 2027) was missing.

value: The built-in pull server removes the need to run your own, though State Configuration retires on 30 September 2027 in favour of Machine Configuration.
reason: Adds the end-of-life note from the same page.

value: Virtual or physical Windows machines, in the cloud or on premises; the page still lists Linux, but Linux support has retired.
reason: The back offered Linux as a current target although Automation DSC for Linux retired on 30 September 2023.

value: Automation DSC for Linux retired on 30 September 2023, so only Windows targets remain supported.
The announcement it links to is about moving to Azure Policy's guest configuration feature, the older name for Machine Configuration.
reason: 'Guest configuration' was unexplained for a newcomer.

value: Its templates set consistency and best practice while maximising security; note that the service retires on 22 February 2027.
reason: The overview carries a retirement note that the primer omitted.

value: Deployment Environments gives developers on-demand infrastructure from approved templates under platform control, but it retires on 22 February 2027, so plan a successor.
reason: Recommending the service without its imminent retirement misleads.

value: Without a `ref` the pipeline uses `refs/heads/main`, whose templates can change; a pinned `ref` keeps one fixed version.
reason: Explanation now says why pinning is needed.

value: Run retention for YAML and classic build pipelines is set in project settings; classic release pipelines still keep their own release retention.
reason: 'Only place ... classic pipelines' clashed with release retention, which is customised on the release pipeline.
